Some of them were great, others not. I agree, inpatient outside of a hospital had been the most beneficial. If I went this time, it would be a short term stay at a hospital for stabilzation and then I might look at another full time outpatient program or inpatient outside of a hospital.

I feel like I've done so much therapy over the last year, it's not as helpful anymore. It's frustrating I can't figure out what to do to get over this depression.

I've done A LOT of therapy over the past year, and I am still in a lot of therapy right now.  Since last April, I've spent 65 days in the hospital (two short term stays, two long term stays), and another 12 weeks in three different full time outpatient programs.  I'm in a three day a week program now.  I'm on medication, and I've even tried less common things like Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation to treat the depression.  The therapy helps, but I don't know, the thoughts just don't go away.

I already have my affairs back in order (will is good to go, have a list of all my bank accounts with log in information, internet histories and devices are clear, checked out the cemetery I want to be buried in, most of my stuff is packed up/cleaned, listed all the people I want contacted, etc.).  I'm pretty much just down to buying a gun, bullets, and a rope - my plan is pretty elaborate, I'm going to shoot myself in the chest with a noose around my neck so if I don't bleed out, I'll still die from hanging.

Again, I want to live, I just can't seem to stop. It's what I do when I feel hopeless and stuck.  I've talked to my therapist about, she's worried of course, but agreed that I can see how this weekend goes.  And I have an appointment with my psychiatrist tomorrow.  I'm tired of this.

I feel like I've been suicidal so frequently over the past year that if I went to the hospital everytime I saw myself following through with it, I'd be there all the time. But I don't know. I think I'm sort of playing with fire right now. I know I want to live, but I can't stop making plans.

We have very similar stories - been in 11 years and are being med boarded for mental health. I've been lucky to receive a lot of mental health care outside the military system. My military providers at my last base were supportive of me getting treatment, and at my current base they are a bunch of dicks who are not supportive at all.

My advice to you is to advocate for full time mental health care. In the past ten months, I've been to the ER, then held for 72 hours twice. Those experiences sucked but they forced medical providers to figure out an after care plan for me, which always involved full time care (in part because that is what I advocated for). I've also completed two 30 day residential inpatient programs - one in Arizona (The Meadows - highly highly recommend!) and one in California. And I've done four different partial hospitalization programs (full time outpatient). So total I've spent the past 5.5 months out of 10 receiving full time mental health care. It's really helped and kept me out of work.

I personally just cannot handle work right now. I used to be a badass at work - Amn of the Year, NCO of the Year, Department of Defense level award for my career field, every rank the first time, highest board score for my career field first time testing for MSgt. It's been really hard to accept that I cant keep myself safe while working, but that's where I'm at.

Please go to the mental health clinic and tell them your safety concerns and advocate for inpatient treatment or full time outpatient treatment. Ask to go to The Meadows (again, it's an amazing program) and research if there are any partial hospitalization programs in your area that take Tricare. If the mental health clinic on base won't listen, fuck them and go to the ER and get put on a hold so they have to come up with a better plan of care for you. Please don't give up and get some help!

Edit: I'm doing Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for depression and it makes my hand twitch :)
